sources.title: PlayStation cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
sources.text: Haven Games to "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation" PlayStation has cancelled Fairgames, the live-service shooter previously in development at its Montreal-based subsidiary Haven Studios. In a statement to Bloomberg , PlayStation said Haven Studios will "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." No jobs have been cut due to the cancellation. According to an email reviewed by Bloomberg, executives Sean Decker and John Doyle informed employees that a recent Fairgames playtest did not meet expectations. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," they said. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." Haven Studios' debut game was announced in 2023, initially scheduled for release last year, and later delayed to Spring 2026. Jade Raymond founded Haven Studios in 2021, and PlayStation Studios acquired the studio in 2022. Following Raymond's departure in May 2025 , executive producer Marie-Eve Danis and Pierre-François Sapinski were appointed co-studio heads. PlayStation started focusing on the live-service market in 2022 by acquiring Bungie for $3.6 billion . Former Sony Interactive Entertainment head Jim Ryan said the company aimed to launch more than ten live-service games by 2026 . Sony reduced the value of its acquisition by $765 million in the 2025/26 fiscal year after Destiny 2 and Marathon underperformed. Earlier this year, Bungie laid off 292 employees and ended development on Destiny 2. Following the game's final update, Bungie announced plans to reinstate vaulted campaigns , raids, and destinations to restore player trust. One of Sony’s most publicised live-service failures was Concord in 2024 , which was withdrawn from sale two weeks after release. Sony subsequently closed its developer Firewalk Studios , along with Neon Koi. Koi. In 2025, Sony cancelled two unannounced live service titles from Bend Studio and Bluepoint Games. The following year, Sony closed Bluepoint, resulting in 70 job losses . Sony Interactive CEO Hideaki Nishino previously said he wanted to "revitalise" live-service projects through a combination of first- and third-party content following its string of failures. "We believe that live service games are content that attracts users on a global level, so we want to continue to revitalise the market through both first-party and third-party content," Nishino said. "We are not only focusing on promoting new releases, but also considering what we can do with older titles in the medium to long term." He continued: "With live service games, it's important to continuously provide something. The genre itself is relatively new, and I think many people are trying various things, so we also want to continue to take on challenges within that context."

Bungie’s Marathon , which launched this year, has had a rough start , but today the studio showed off some new features coming in a December update , including a new co-op PvE roguelite mode and a PvP deathmatch mode. sources.title: Sony cancels another live service game ahead of release, but at least there won't be any layoffs this time
sources.text: Fairgames was revealed in 2023, but nothing more was ever seen of it. A Bloomberg report says Fairgames, a PvP heist shooter announced by Haven Studios and Sony in 2023 , has been cancelled. In something of a surprising twist, a PlayStation rep told the site there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation, as Haven will "shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." While it was announced three years ago, work on Fairgames appears to have started even further back, in 2021. Just a couple months after her high-profile split with Google Stadia , Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond announced the formation of Haven Studios , which was "working on an unannounced new IP for PlayStation." In 2022, right around the time former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan was talking about launching 12 live service games by 2025, Sony acquired the studio outright; a year after that, Fairplay was revealed to the world. But things have not gone smoothly since then. Helldivers 2 was a massive hit, but seven of those planned games were cancelled before release . Of the remaining games, one was Marathon , which endures but has not lived up to expectations, and another was Concord , one of the most famously disastrous game launches in years, which was taken offline less than two weeks after it launched, never to return. A live-service spinoff of the Horizon series, Hunters Gathering, was also reportedly rebooted after negative feedback from playtests . A partial accounting of canned multiplayer projects: The Concord catastrophe in particular seemed to shake Sony, which began reversing its live service strategy just a few months later. Fairgames itself looked to be in trouble in 2025 when Raymond departed Haven , reportedly after an external playtest left PlayStation leadership "concerned about how the game was received and its progress." The Bloomberg report says a more recent large-scale playtest produced similar results. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email sent to Haven Studios employees. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." The one bright spot to the cancellation is that no jobs will be cut because of it: A Sony rep told Bloomberg that Haven "will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." sources.title: PlayStation's embattled shooter Fairgames has finally been cancelled, a new report says, as live service push withers away
sources.text: After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff. According to a new Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore new creative opportunities". Fairgames was initially announced in 2023 as one of several in-development live service games, as part of an initiative by former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan to create more than a dozen games that generate recurring revenue . Most of those titles were cancelled before they were even revealed, and those that made it out, such as Concord, flopped severely . Even Sony darling Guerrilla Games seemingly can't make it work, with recent reports saying the studio's Horizon Hunters Gathering - initially envisioned as a live service spin on the robo dinosaur series - will now shift into a more traditional co-op structure without live service elements. That's assuming the team can show a revamped version of the game to executives by December. The news of Fairgames' cancellation isn't surprising. The game has had a tumultuous development journey ever since its reveal. Initially set for release in 2025, the game was soon pushed back to 2026 , following the departure of studio founder Jade Raymond . Though Sony later reiterated its commitment to its remaining in-development live service titles , Fairgames was never shown to the public again. That same year, game director Daniel Drapeau left Haven - another key departure suggesting the game had difficulties and might not see release. Throughout that time, Fairgames has reportedly been reworked multiple times, with a plan for it to be re-revealed under a new name. That name is believed to be Break In, linked to a trademark Sony filed in May , but with the project cancelled, we may never know if that was the case.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Nintendo Defends Decision to Cut Mario and Yoshi Easter Eggs From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Hidden away inside Hyrule Castle, the game's original 1998 version included a wall of portraits that featured Mario, Luigi, Peach, Bowser, and Yoshi artwork taken from Super Mario 64. Visit the same area in Nintendo's newly-launched Switch 2 version, however, and all references to the Mushroom Kingdom have been removed. On a similar note, a selection of Zelda: Twilight Princess artwork has also been cut, having been snuck in when Ocarina of Time was re-released on 3DS. Now, Nintendo has addressed its choice to remove these Easter eggs — and said that what was once a more "carefree" approach within Nintendo to referencing other games has been reconsidered. "Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal," legendary Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma told Game Informer . "Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing. "But looking at it now... given the overall way that we're creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time." While some fans might feel like it's a shame to see this more carefree attitude to Easter eggs is gone, it's fair to point out that Mario 64 Easter eggs (or Skyward Sword ones, for that matter) would make less sense today. Mario 64 was launched on the same platform as Ocarina of Time, of course, while Skyward Sword was released contemporaneously with the game's 3DS port. (Maybe Switch 2 just needs a new Mario game to actually arrive?) "I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game," Aonuma continued, "and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that... [But] you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way." "No hard feelings there," commented Skyward Sword director Hidemaro Fujibayashi, who returned as a producer for this remake. And one Mario reference does still survive via Talon — a character who is an obvious nod to Mario with his bushy moustache, plus red and blue overalls. Check out his necklace, and you'll see his golden Bowser charm remains intact, all these years later. Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has previously discussed the idea of the company's different franchises crossing over , and said that he wasn't a fan — except when it is Pikmin , which he wants to include wherever possible. Earlier today, Nintendo revealed that Ocarina of Time had already shifted 5.2 million copies and become the Switch 2's fastest-selling game so far. Meanwhile, players have been having fun in-game by performing everything from Linkin Park to the Titanic theme on ocarina . You can read our review of the game here , or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. sources.title: 10 Ways Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is Better Than the Original
sources.text: The original The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time has been certified as the highest-rated video game ever for a long time now. 2026’s Remake , however, has immediately climbed the charts and is currently this year’s top-rated title. The question then becomes, “Which one is actually better overall?” For my personal two cents, I still give the OG a slight edge. At the same time, that doesn’t take anything away from the Remake. In fact, 2026’s version of Ocarina is actually better in some cases. Let’s take a look at ten different ways Nintendo was able to take the classic and somehow improve on some aspects. Most obviously, the graphical and performance upgrades in OOT Remake are substantial. This isn’t a surprise at all since the OG is from the ’90s, but Remake still smashed it out of the park in terms of design and tone as well. Despite some concerns over glossy character models during the pre-launch phase of the game, the new art direction is constantly breathtaking and pulled off masterfully. Standouts are Lake Hylia with its gorgeous water effects, and Ganondorf’s Castle, which straight up looks like it’s ripped out of Mordor in Lord of the Rings. The hardest thing about going back for the original version of OOT is the control scheme and camera. Sure, the visuals are dated, but there’s a definite charm and style to them as well. The controls are just… old. This barrier to entry being removed in Zelda: Ocarina Remake was crucial to it succeeding in modern times. Thankfully, the right-stick camera works beautifully (though Z-Target centering was still kept in as well). Sword combat and shield blocking are fluid and snappy. Perhaps most importantly, however, is that projectile aiming can now be toggled between standard camera control and inverted. The 1998 game only offered inverted aiming, which is a total no-go for many modern gamers. There’s a certain charm in figuring out the auto-ledge jumping in N64 Ocarina, but it’s no surprise that having an actual, dedicated jump button in Remake is a massive improvement. Back in the day, Link’s jumping mechanics were the best Nintendo could muster, and we learned to adapt to them. But in 2026, not having an actual jump would’ve been a crime. This new ability also leads to some fun location and dungeon redesigns since Link can reach higher ledges and areas than ever before. A lot of players hopping into Remake (myself included) know almost everything about the N64 game. When picking up Remake, I wondered just how 1:1 everything would be, including things like gold skulltulas and room layouts. To my surprise, it was a blast to explore the new game and learn that many locations had been shuffled around or changed entirely. And this isn’t just a “better” change because it’s different. Instead, there are now several examples of things being placed more thoughtfully and satisfyingly in the game world. Take, for example, the Kokiri Sword, which now takes a little more parkour action to collect. I may know the lore and story of Zelda: Ocarina of Time better than any other video game. Upon recently replaying the OG, however, it’s funny how much of the narrative is a little bit underexplained. Case in point: the Triforce itself is shoddily explained, making it less impactful when considering why everyone seems to care so much about it. In Remake, most characters have a plethora of added or tweaked dialogue. A lot of this added exposition serves the game extremely well, making the stakes clearer and even giving us additional lore and info along the way. I didn’t expect to learn even more about Hyrule and the plot of the game in 2026, but the Remake gave me the opportunity. Growing up, we’d often have to make up video game character voices in our heads. Fully voice-acted games weren’t the norm yet. Aside from Navi shouting her classic “Hey!” and “Listen!” lines, the rest of the OG cast was relegated to grunts, screams, laughs, and moans. Hearing immediate narration voice-over when booting up Remake is a trip. For the most part, I found all the actor choices on-point, too. My personal standout is the English dub for Kaepora Gaebora, the Guiding Owl, played by Frank Todaro. There were doubts that Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s legendary soundtrack could be improved, but it somehow was. Of course, this is in large part due to the songs now being fully orchestrated, which was not an option on the Nintendo 64. Still, it wouldn’t have been hard to mess this one up with how beloved 1998’s tunes still are to this day. Thankfully, the full orchestration is gorgeous, as the new, sweeping melodies pack home way more emotion than ever before. Special shout-out to Saria’s Song, which comes back several times in a surprising, haunting fashion. While I wouldn’t say every dungeon was improved in the Remake, several were still fundamentally made better. In general, they’re all a bit more straightforward, which is nice for first-time players who aren’t used to retro game design. At the same time, simpler isn’t always better. In the case of dungeons like the Water Temple and Jabu-Jabu’s Belly, however, streamlining was the move. The migraine-inducing original Water Temple is reworked just enough that it went from my least favorite in the OG, to possibly my actual favorite in Remake. Most, if not all, of the dungeons are essentially at least on par with the original versions. The handful that actually made things better then stand out that much more this time around. While there aren’t too many challenging boss or enemy encounters in Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, fighting everything is still more fun than ever. This is thanks to many tweaks to encounter structure and entire enemy movesets. For example, King Dodongo now summons baby Dodongos during phases of the boss fight. Twinrova has an additional, arena-spanning spin attack. It’s a blast to have to reconsider and relearn these fights (and also practice them in the added Hall of Fallen Foes mode). sources.title: GTA VI will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming for Xbox One consoles
sources.text: Rockstar Games confirms GTA VI will run at 30fps across all consoles. Rockstar Games confirms GTA VI will run at 30fps across all consoles. Rockstar Games is making Grand Theft Auto VI available on Xbox Cloud Gaming when it launches next week. While you’d normally assume that would mean Grand Theft Auto VI would be available to stream on phones, PCs, the web, Xbox consoles, and even TVs, it appears to be restricted to just Xbox Series X / S and Xbox One consoles. That does mean that anyone with an older Xbox One console can stream Grand Theft Auto VI instead of having to upgrade to a PS5 or Xbox Series S / X console to play. Rockstar notes that Xbox Cloud Gaming will use the Xbox Series S graphics settings to stream to Xbox consoles. Xbox’s own announcement blog post only mentions Xbox Cloud Gaming streaming for Xbox Series X / S and Xbox One owners. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma says the cloud deal for Grand Theft Auto VI is “the first step in our new 10-year strategic partnership with Take-Two.” Sharma also says the game is “the most pre-ordered game ever on Microsoft Store.” Microsoft is also planning to add Grand Theft Auto V , Red Dead Redemption 2 , and more to Xbox Cloud Gaming in “the coming months.” What this all means is that Microsoft effectively has an exclusive on streaming Grand Theft Auto VI from the cloud for launch, albeit only to Xbox consoles. I originally reported last month that Microsoft had secured exclusive Grand Theft Auto VI cloud streaming rights, but Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball revealed on X that Microsoft wouldn’t be streaming Grand Theft Auto VI exclusively. While Microsoft’s contract might not specifically state exclusive, the end result is exclusive cloud gaming on Xbox, for now. Sony may well eventually announce its own cloud streaming plans for the game, but Rockstar Games notes that Grand Theft Auto VI “will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.” That’s not cloud streaming, though. I also initially reported that Grand Theft Auto VI would be available to stream on PC, simply because the entire point of Xbox Cloud Gaming is to make games available on Xbox consoles, TVs, PCs, and the web. It’s strange to see a rare exception for Grand Theft Auto VI , but not entirely surprising. Perhaps Microsoft will eventually be able to stream the PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI whenever it launches. Rockstar Games also confirms Grand Theft Auto VI will run at 30fps across PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S / X consoles. The main advantage of a PS5 Pro is ray-traced shadows and support for PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). Update, November 10th : Article updated with comments from Xbox.

A possibilidade é uma novidade importante, já que o console pertence à geração passada e não consegue executar o jogo nativamente. Nos consoles mais recentes da Microsoft, GTA 6 será executado diretamente no hardware. O Xbox Series X oferecerá a experiência nativa de console com melhor desempenho gráfico, enquanto o Series S será a opção mais acessível para jogar sem depender de streaming. Já no Xbox One, o funcionamento será diferente: o game será executado em servidores da Microsoft e transmitido pela internet por meio do Xbox Cloud Gaming. Nesse formato, o console não precisa processar o jogo, apenas reproduzir a transmissão. Segundo a Microsoft, a versão transmitida pela nuvem utilizará as configurações gráficas do Xbox Series S — e, assim como em todos os consoles, também rodará a 30 FPS . Além disso, a empresa confirmou que jogadores de mercados compatíveis poderão comprar tempo de jogo na nuvem a partir de 11 de novembro, sem precisar de uma assinatura do Game Pass. Se quiser saber quanto custa a hora da nuvem no Game Pass, clique aqui ! Por fim, a companhia afirmou estar animada para levar GTA 6 a mais jogadores no lançamento e também planeja adicionar outros títulos da Rockstar ao serviço, incluindo GTA 5 e Red Dead Redemption 2 . Vale lembrar que o jogo precisa ser adquirido separadamente para acessar a transmissão . Apesar de GTA 6 chegar ao Xbox One por streaming, o jogo infelizmente não poderá ser executado no PS4 . O console da Sony não receberá uma versão nativa do título, e a Rockstar não anunciou suporte ao jogo por meio de serviços de nuvem da PlayStation. A diferença está justamente na forma de funcionamento do Xbox Cloud Gaming. Como o processamento acontece nos servidores da Microsoft, o Xbox One não precisa ter potência suficiente para executar GTA 6 localmente. A PlayStation também oferece streaming de jogos em nuvem por meio dos planos mais completos do PS Plus Premium, mas a disponibilidade varia de acordo com a região e o catálogo de títulos compatíveis. Lembrando que o mesmo nível é chamado de PS Plus Deluxe no Brasil e não possui a disponibilidade de jogos em nuvem. Até o momento, não há confirmação de que GTA 6 será oferecido dessa maneira no serviço. Portanto, entre os consoles da geração passada, apenas o Xbox One terá acesso a GTA 6 por meio de streaming na nuvem. No caso do PS4, os jogadores não poderão aproveitar o lançamento, já que não existe uma versão compatível anunciada para o aparelho. Lembrando que GTA 6 será lançado em 19 de novembro de 2026 para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S. O título será disponibilizado exclusivamente nos consoles de atual geração inicialmente — mas é bastante provável que uma versão de PC também chegue no primeiro trimestre de 2027, segundo fortes rumores que circularam recentemente . sources.text: Grand Theft Auto V is the reigning game of all time. One of gamingâs most undeniable cultural exports. An ugly game that casts one unbelievable shadow. A title so massive, itâs become damn near impossible to recreate without burning down your development studio in 2026. Revisiting it in the lead-up to GTA VI âs release later this year has been illuminating in many ways, but the thing Iâm perhaps most struck by about the 2013 hit is how miserable it is. What a fascinating thing to exist in the supposed upper echelon of the gaming pantheon. GTA V is filled with all kinds of missions and objectivesâthe stuff that modern gaming parlance constantly calls “content.” Really, it turns everything into content for you to check off. It’s got big missions and small ones. Simple, boring ones that occasionally lull you to sleep. Distractions like tennis and drag racing. And, on the other end, massive, multi-part setpieces that get the blood pumping a little more efficiently. A gulf separates these sequences. Sometimes I’m little more than a glorified cabbie, at other times a glorified avatar of the âAmerican dreamââa ball of boredom, rage, and discontent at The Way Things Are, armed with a rifle aimed at nothing in particular. Lots of it feels utterly meaningless. Stealing the occasional getaway vehicle and quietly parking it in a nearby lot often counts as a mission, one I hate after doing it multiple times in my ~50 hours revisiting GTA V . Not that its more pulse-pounding action is especially noteworthy either. The game’s crosshair, for example, is wholly unremarkable. It’s just a dot. A dot that, by default, magnetizes to the often nameless nobodies on the other end of your barrel, as if to smooth any friction that could possibly arise in the instant between when you see a foe and when you pull the trigger on your weapon of choice.Â Many other shooters feature different crosshairs depending on the weapon. A grenade launcher might suggest an arc. A sniper rifle, too. A shotgun blast has a wider spread, and a crosshair usually indicates its range. But time and time again, GTA V plays it cool, calm, and detached with its minimalist crosshair. It doesn’t want to bore you with calculating distances and trajectories. It wants you to endlessly put holes in cops, gangsters, hillbillies, rival drug enterprises, federal agents, clowns, aliens, and everything in between, while occasionally piloting several classes of vehicle in increasingly linear scenarios. It doesn’t feel wholly good or bad; it feels likeâ¦nothing.Â Driving around the state of San Andreas and shooting things feels like nothing . A kind of nothing that quicklyâ easily âfills dozens of hours. Like a chore. Maybe that’s the best way to describe GTA V . Well, if itâs going to be such a chore, it feels, at least, like GTA V should aim that tedium at some larger point, shouldn’t it? It kind of does. Each of its endeavors, be it a mundane task, an odd job to rustle up some cash, or a riotous heist spilled out on the streets of not-LA, does in fact feel pointed. Compulsive, even. At least in part because they feel like the backdrop for the gameâs occasionally devastating musings that hit with the force of, well, a getaway vehicle.Â The most consequential series of missions among GTA V ‘s errands is largely divorced from the thrust of its campaign. Itâs got nothing to do with heists and has nothing to do with two-thirds of the gameâs playable trio. Itâs got nothing to do with the city of Los Santos, even. Far up in the middle of Nowhere, Blaine County, is an unsavory duo called the Minute Men, who are on a collision course with a similarly ugly force by the name of Trevor Phillipsâa walking, talking (usually swearing) cancer and truly one of the most detestable protagonists a game has ever saddled a player with.Â The Minute Menâs contributions to GTA V are small but important. Over a triptych of morally repugnant descents into darkness that only Trevor can take on, they try to prove the righteousness of their cause. In a move that felt like a cavity opening in my soul, Trevor rides along with Joe and Josef, two members of the âCivil Border Patrol,â as they chase down and detain Mexican-American citizens across the countryside. Or as one of them says, in his native Russian on American soil, âWell-motivated people, eager to do low-level jobs at any wage to support their families.âÂ These missions are, like the rest of GTA V âs offerings, pretty unremarkable in their construction. You chase after these poor souls in a patrol vehicleâa park rangerâs van with hardly a new splash of paintâtase them (another drab crosshair) and eventually escort them back to the vehicle, where they are subsequently driven to a somewhat ambiguous fate. The whole thing would only run about 15 minutes if the missions were stitched together, and ends with little fanfare. All in all, these excursions with the Civil Border Patrol are a perfect microcosm of what GTA V actually excels at: being a banal cascade of senseless violence and bigotry, bookended by a smug but empty wink. A shockingly vivid reflection of our depravity and our inability to break from it. A post-modern vision of what passes for a video game and what can be fun about it.Â Many of GTA V âs most memorable moments echo this particular sensibility, as has become customary of the franchise, which has satirized America and its long-running series of systemic failures over the past 25 years. The mission “Friend Request,” which involves another of the gameâs protagonists, named Michael, breaking into the headquarters of a Facebook analog called Life Invader, is a perfect example. In it Michael, and thus the player, live out what has become, in the years since the gameâs release, an even more entertaining fantasy, making a very public example of a tech mogul with an inflated ego and a penchant for flagrant violations of child labor laws. sources.text: Both platforms encourage players to pre-load the game to minimise potential delays and crashes on launch day Grand Theft Auto 6 has become the most pre-ordered game on the PlayStation Store and Microsoft Store. Sensor Tower's GTA 6 sales tracker currently estimates nearly 9.69 million pre-orders worldwide, generating $942 million in revenue. These figures have risen significantly in one week. On November 7, the tracker reported nearly eight million pre-orders and $751 million in revenue. GTA 6 pre-orders have exceeded expectations for Rockstar's parent company Take-Two Interactive . "[We cannot] disclose the numbers, but the point that we're making is our prior expectations obviously were aligned with our guidance, and the pre-orders are far exceeding our original expectations," Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick recently told GamesIndustry.biz . "We're maintaining our guidance, because the release is only 10 days away and we'll know a lot more after the release." In Take-Two's recent Q2 results , Zelnick said the company expects to "deliver a historic year" as a result of GTA 6's launch. Since November 10, GTA 6 has been available to pre-load on PlayStation and Xbox. Both platforms recommend pre-loading to help prevent crashes and delays on launch day, much like what happened with Hollow Knight: Silksong last year . GamesIndustry.biz recently consulted experts on whether GTA 6 could overwhelm internet traffic and if pre-loading will help manage download demand before next week's release. GamesDiscoverCo newsletter author Simon Carless said that "having an extra nine days to gradually send out the bulk of the data to players' computers is vital. There still might be a Day 1 patch/extra download, but if so, it'll be very incremental." Investor and strategic advisor Joost van Dreunen suggested the download bottleneck could still come on launch day, when "tens of millions day-of buyers, not a few hundred thousand" will be downloading the game.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 is 'the most pre-ordered' game of all time on both Xbox and PlayStation
sources.text: On PC, however, GTA 6 remains among the least pre-ordered games of all time because, well, you know. It goes without saying (yet here I am saying it) that Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to be huge. We don't really have a sense as to just how huge at this point: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has boasted that GTA 6 preorder numbers are " unprecedented ," but he's refused to provide specifics because "the raw numbers could be potentially misleading." But huge, for sure. Now both Sony and Xbox have joined in the 'gonna be huge' chorus, each of them announcing that preorders for GTA 6 are, definitionally, unprecedented . "Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony proclaimed on the PlayStation Blog . "Given this unprecedented demand, we’ve joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they’re ready to play on launch day. We’ve also adopted a rolling midnight launch by country, beginning at 12:00AM NZDT in New Zealand and running across the globe as respective countries hit midnight on November 19." Xbox made a similar announcement on its own website, calling GTA 6 "the most pre-ordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store" and encouraging users to begin preloading as soon as possible because of "the unprecedented demand" for the game. Alongside Xbox Series X/S consoles, Xbox said GTA 6 will also be playable on Xbox One consoles through Xbox Cloud Gaming. That service is also available on PC, but Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Bell confirmed in October that GTA 6 will not be streamable on our platform . But while nobody is serving up specifics on the number of GTA 6 copies sold via preorder, we do have a rough indicator of how much money Take-Two expects to make when it comes out of the gate. The publisher is projecting net bookings of $3.35 to $3.5 billion for its current fiscal quarter, "driven by the groundbreaking release of Grand Theft Auto 6" on November 19. That's roughly double what Take-Two took in during the same quarter in its previous year, when it reported net bookings of $1.76 billion. "The launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is ten days away and, with pre-orders continuing to reach unprecedented levels, we expect to deliver an historic year for our company," Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said during yesterday's quarterly financial report. sources.text: Soul Reaver 2 and Freedom Wars Remastered join PlayStation Plus Premium. This month, embark on an inspiring mission of human connection in Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, assemble a one-of-a-kind crew as you explore the open sea in Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii, navigate the cult-controlled ruins, natural caves, and nuclear bunkers of a green and unpleasant British countryside in Atomfall, or explore a vast world map with an abundance of captivating locations in Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake. All these titles and more are available in November’s PlayStation Plus Game Catalog lineup*. Meanwhile, Soul Reaver 2 and Freedom Wars Remastered land into PlayStation Plus Premium. The full lineup will be available to play from November 17, unless otherwise noted. Embark on an inspiring mission of human connection beyond the UCA. Join Sam for the next chapter of his journey as he attempts to connect Australia to the Chiral Network. Navigate a living environment through day and night cycles, natural disasters including earthquakes, sandstorms and forest fires, and Timefall – a rain that instantly ages everything it touches. To traverse this dangerous landscape, you’ll need to build new types of infrastructure, master specialised equipment, and confront (or evade) the otherworldly creatures that roam the fractured world. Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii | PS5, PS4 A new legend begins as you step into the steel toe boots of Goro Majima, a man who has lost his memory and reinvents himself as a pirate on the open sea. Embark on an over-the-top, modern-day pirate adventure with an ex-yakuza, now pirate captain and his crew as they engage in exhilarating combat on land and sea in the hunt for lost memories and a legendary treasure. Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii will be available November 24 in the US, the UK and Japan. A survival-action game inspired by real-life events, Atomfall is set five years after the Windscale nuclear disaster in Northern England. Explore the fictional quarantine zone, scavenge, craft, barter, fight and talk your way through a British countryside setting filled with bizarre characters, mysticism, cults, and rogue government agencies. From Rebellion, the studio behind Sniper Elite and Zombie Army, Atomfall will challenge you to solve the dark mystery of what really happened. A stunning reimagining of the beloved RPG masterpiece and narrative beginning to The Erdrick Trilogy. Years ago, the great hero Ortega bid farewell to his wife and child as he set off on a quest to defeat the villainous Archfiend, Baramos. Ortega failed his quest, and Baramos still threatens the world. Now, on their 16th birthday, Ortega’s only child is summoned by the king of Aliahan and entrusted with a mission of the highest import: to take on Ortega’s quest, vanquish Baramos and save the world. In Trepang2, you play as an escaped soldier who has no memories of their past life, but is infused with supernatural abilities. Revenge is on your mind, and you’ll stop at nothing to get what you want. Deliver devastating punches, sneak around in the shadows, wield explosive weapons, and give the bad guys a taste of their own medicine. Fight back, find the truth and face a threat even deadlier than yourself. Trepang2 will be available November 24 in the US and the UK. Experience the full intensity of the 2026 MotoGP Championship with all the official riders, teams, bikes and tracks in a more authentic way: for the first time, the real-world results dynamically update Riders Ratings, directly influencing in-game performance throughout the season. Step into the spotlight and track your journey with dazzling Collectible Cards celebrating your progress. MotoGP 26 will be available November 24 in the US and the UK. Join the ever-expanding experience of Hell Let Loose – a hardcore World War Two first person shooter with epic battles of 100 players with infantry, tanks, artillery, a dynamically shifting front line and a unique resource based RTS-inspired meta-game. Take to the battlefield in 50 vs 50 multiplayer across huge maps. Choose one of 14 playable roles within infantry, recon and armour unit types, each equipped with different weapons, vehicles and equipment. Play as an Officer, Scout, Machine Gunner, Medic, Engineer, Tank Commander and more to experience every aspect of World War II combat. Hell Let Loose will be available tomorrow, November 11 in the US, the UK and November 12 in Japan. Cricket 26 – The Official Game of the Ashes | PS5, PS4 Featuring the all-new Management Career, a bigger and better Pro Team, in-depth Ashes mode, and expanded control on and off the field from enhanced gameplay and in-depth strategies – Cricket 26 is The Ultimate Showdown. Cricket 26 – The Official Game of the Ashes will be available November 24 in the US and the UK. Soul Reaver 2 | PS5, PS4 In this sequel to the critically acclaimed Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver, reassume the role of Raziel, and battle back through the currents of time into pivotal, dangerous eras of Nosgoth’s past in your relentless pursuit of Kain. Encounter new enemies as you unearth the mysteries of Nosgoth’s ancient races, and expose the schemes that lie behind the corruption of the Pillars. In a distant future where all resources on earth have been depleted, being alive is a sin by itself. Born into a one-million-year prison sentence, you must survive deadly missions to earn any hope of freedom. Die in prison or live on the battlefield. The choice is yours. Use your most trusted weapon, your Thorn, to dominate the battlefield. Stand alongside your allies and your warden cyborg Accessory to face off against powerful enemies. *PlayStation Plus Game Catalog and PlayStation Plus Premium/Deluxe lineups may differ by region. Neste mês, embarque em uma missão inspiradora de conexão humana em Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, reúna uma tripulação única enquanto navega o alto-mar em Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii, explore ruínas controladas por seitas, cavernas naturais e bunkers nucleares de uma zona rural britânica inóspita e coberta de vegetação em Atomfall, ou explore um vasto mapa repleto de locais cativantes em Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake. Para atravessar esta paisagem perigosa, você precisará construir novos tipos de infraestrutura, dominar equipamentos especializados e enfrentar (ou evitar) as criaturas sobrenaturais que vagam pelo mundo fragmentado. Há muitos anos, o grande herói Ortega despediu-se da esposa e do filho ao partir em uma jornada para derrotar o vilão Baramos, o arquidemônio. Ortega falhou em sua missão, e Baramos ainda ameaça o mundo. Desfira golpes devastadores, esconda-se nas sombras, empunhe armas explosivas e faça os vilões provarem do próprio veneno. Revide, descubra a verdade e enfrente uma ameaça ainda mais mortal do que você. Vivencie toda a intensidade do Campeonato de MotoGP de 2026 com todos os pilotos, equipes, motos e circuitos oficiais de forma mais autêntica: pela primeira vez, os resultados do mundo real atualizam dinamicamente as classificações dos pilotos, influenciando diretamente o desempenho no jogo ao longo da temporada. Entre na batalha em partidas de vários jogadores de 50 vs. 50 em mapas enormes. Escolha uma das 14 missões na infantaria, os tipos de unidades de reconhecimento e armadura, cada uma equipada com armas, veículos e equipamentos diferentes. Jogue como oficial, batedor, artilheiro, médico, engenheiro, comandante de tanque e muito mais para vivenciar todos os aspectos dos combates da Segunda Guerra Mundial. Soul Reaver 2 | PS5, PS4 Nesta sequência do aclamado Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver, assuma novamente o papel de Raziel e lute para voltar, atravessando as areias do tempo, às épocas decisivas e perigosas do passado de Nosgoth em sua busca implacável por Kain. Enfrente novos inimigos enquanto desvenda os mistérios das antigas civilizações de Nosgoth e revele os planos que estão por trás da corrupção dos Pilares. Em um futuro distante, onde todos os recursos da Terra se esgotaram, estar vivo já é um pecado por si só. Condenado a uma pena de prisão de um milhão de anos, você precisa sobreviver a missões letais para ter qualquer esperança de liberdade. Morra na prisão ou viva no combate. A escolha é sua. sources.text: Black Forest Games has split from THQ Nordic after nearly 10 years of ownership, the companies announced. The Offenburg, Germany-based developer was acquired by THQ Nordic in August 2017. Following a management buyout by the leadership of Black Forest Games, the two companies will pursue different business priorities. Both companies, however, will continue to collaborate on projects within game development going forward. Black Forest Games, meanwhile, has founded joined the newly established Third Signal , an independent group of game studios making premium games, as a founding member and co-owner of the group. “Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred,” said Third Signal founder and CEO Andreas Tobler in a press release. “Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life.” Black Forest Games co-founder and CEO Adrian Goersch added, “We are grateful to THQ Nordic and Embracer for nine good years and the games we made together. sources.text: Black Forest Games - the studio that remade the first two cult-classic Destroy All Humans games - has spun out from under former owners THQ Nordic and Embracer Group. The Destroy All Humans remaker won its newfound independence through a management buyout, and wasted no time at all in co-founding Third Signal, which is described as a new group of independent studios that'll eventually provide help and resources to other indie teams. "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of 50, not 500. Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life," Third Signal CEO Andreas Tobler said in a press release. Black Forest Games was one of Embracer Group's earliest high-profile acquisitions almost a decade ago, before the company swallowed up countless big names (Lord of the Rings, Tomb Raider, Kingdom Come: Deliverance , more) in the following years and spat back a bunch shortly after. Most infamously, Embracer sold Gearbox and Borderlands during its massive internal restructuring in 2024. It doesn't sound like Black Forest split with the rights to the Destroy All Humans series or its permanently mean alien protag Crypto, but the studio has said it's still working with THQ Nordic in some capacity. The original Destroy All Humans run nosedived wildly in quality after the second game, so I'm not sure how exciting a remake of, let's say, Destroy All Humans: Big Willy Unleashed would be nowadays, though I'd definitely be interested in seeing Crypto again in another ridiculously silly, sometimes rude and anarchic adventure.

sources.text: GTA 6 ganha novo teaser e inicia preload após recorde de pré-vendas A poucos dias da estreia de GTA 6 , a Sony acaba de anunciar que o PlayStation 5 ultrapassou oficialmente a marca de 100 milhões de unidades vendidas. O resultado pode ter sido impulsionado pela expectativa em torno do novo jogo da Rockstar, que chega ao mercado em novembro — embora isso seja mera especulação da nossa parte. Segundo os dados divulgados pela empresa, o console atingiu o marco em 10 de novembro. Isso significa que pelo menos 2,1 milhões de unidades foram enviadas desde 30 de setembro, quando a Sony havia informado que o PS5 acumulava 97,9 milhões de consoles vendidos . Lançado em novembro de 2020, o PlayStation 5 precisou de quase seis anos para ultrapassar a marca de 100 milhões de unidades vendidas. O resultado é semelhante ao registrado pelo PlayStation 4, que atingiu o mesmo número em junho de 2019 — cerca de cinco anos e sete meses após sua estreia. Com isso, o PS5 entra para um grupo restrito de consoles que ultrapassaram a marca de 100 milhões de unidades comercializadas. Até o momento, apenas sete videogames alcançaram esse resultado, todos fabricados pela Nintendo ou pela Sony. Confira a lista: Apesar de ter alcançado um número expressivo, o ritmo de vendas do PS5 vem diminuindo gradualmente, como costuma acontecer com consoles que chegam ao sexto ano de mercado — mas isso pode mudar com a chegada iminente de GTA 6 . A proximidade do lançamento de GTA 6 pode ter contribuído para o aumento recente na procura pelo PlayStation 5. Como o novo jogo da Rockstar é um dos lançamentos mais aguardados da indústria, parte do público pode estar aproveitando o período para comprar o console antes da estreia. Embora a Sony não tenha confirmado uma relação direta entre o desempenho comercial do PS5 e a chegada do game, o aumento de pelo menos 2,1 milhões de unidades enviadas desde o fim de setembro coincide com a reta final da campanha de lançamento. Outro fator que pode influenciar as vendas é a expectativa de que GTA 6 seja um dos principais jogos da geração atual. Como o título chegará ao PS5 e ao Xbox Series X|S, consumidores que ainda não possuem um dos consoles podem decidir fazer a compra para jogar a novidade. Enquanto o PS5 continua vendendo, o sucessor do console ainda pode demorar alguns anos para chegar ao mercado. No início deste ano, David Gibson, analista sênior da MST Financial, publicou um relatório indicando que o ciclo de vida do aparelho atual deve ser mais longo do que algumas previsões anteriores sugeriam. “A Sony espera que o ciclo de vida do PS5 seja prolongado, e o lançamento do PS6 provavelmente será adiado por mais tempo do que muitos esperavam”, afirmou Gibson em sua análise. A possibilidade de um lançamento mais distante também foi reforçada pelo CEO da Sony, Hiroki Totoki. Durante teleconferência sobre os resultados financeiros mais recentes da companhia, o executivo afirmou que a empresa ainda não havia definido uma data para a chegada do PlayStation 6. Mesmo sem uma previsão oficial, alguns analistas trabalham com a possibilidade de que o novo videogame seja lançado em meados de 2028. A avaliação de Gibson, no entanto, aponta que o sucessor do PS5 pode chegar ainda mais tarde do previsto por conta da crise de chips que encareceu consideravelmente componentes de hardware. sources.title: Side Effects Guaranteed in the First DLC For The Outer Worlds 2, Coming December 2
sources.text: A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation. All signs point to foul play, especially the puddle of what was most likely a person. You recover a video message left by the captain of the vessel, who explains that the crew has been contaminated with something while on a heist that will cause explosive cell death unless they find a cure. And by explosive cell death, she means more like a… “liquefaction”. By the looks of the puddle on the floor: liquefaction indeed. The stakes are set for the release of the first of a two-part narrative DLC expansion of The Outer Worlds 2 on December 2. In Side Effects Guaranteed , the video message you found leads you to Gordon Hazen, one of the leading agents in Sub Rosa, a criminal organization made up of like-minded individuals who have chosen to live their lives stealing from the various factions instead of working for them. Gordon in turn sends you to Elysium Valley, a new region on Eden that is home to a settlement of former Protectorate subjects that have been forgotten by their Protectorate leaders. He believes they may have the answers to saving his crew. He personally favors diplomacy over violence but needs you to do whatever you need to in order to get the information he needs. But Gordon isn’t the only one with interest in Elysium Valley. Another Sub Rosa agent, Algernon Lankester, wants to recruit you to help him exploit the subjects for his own personal gain. The fate of the subjects, the frozen Sub Rosa agents, and the future of Sub Rosa itself is up for you, our intrepid Commander, to decide. A new narrative story is not all that will be coming when Side Effects Guaranteed launches in a few weeks, however. Along with the new region of Elysium Valley to explore, players will encounter new threats like vicious canids and primal sprats. What’s a primal sprat? Just a normal sprat, but about 100 times the size. Surely, they’re just as friendly and forgiving of all the time you “accidentally” shot their much smaller cousins while exploring Arcadia. With these new threats comes the ability to make your Commander even stronger and, of course, more flawed (but in a good way). The level cap will increase from 30 to 36, bringing more skill points to broaden your build. Being able to go to level 36 also means there are three more perks you can acquire, with 15 brand new perks being added into the mix. Four new flaws will also be introduced that can change how your Commander plays, like “Lethally Tolerant,” a flaw that recognizes your built-up resistance to chemicals so your max toxicity will increase. This is great in the moment, but if you ever experience a Toxicity Crash, you will die instantly. Another example is “Must Have Been the Wind,” which will mark an “assassination target” for a combat group. Killing the target will grant a 20% damage and speed buff until the combat ends, but failing to do so or attacking someone who isn’t the target applies a 10% damage and speed debuff to the player for 30 seconds. Truly rewards that come with great risks. Side Effects Guaranteed will also see new weapons, new armors, and new outfits for each of the companions, as well as a brand-new Sub Rosa-run radio station featuring 20 new songs for the game. For those who want to jump straight to the action in the DLC, a new alternate starting point is being added to the main menu when you choose a new game that will allow you to start with a custom save that lands you at the start of the DLC. Start the game, allot your skill and perk points, and enjoy Side Effects Guaranteed right away! This jam-packed adventure with a deep story and systems to build your ideal commander will set up the next DLC for The Outer Worlds 2 that will be coming in Spring of 2027, and choices made will directly impact the next DLC. Part one of this overarching expansion story, Side Effects Guaranteed , will release on December 2 for $14.99, or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2 .

stories.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders Review
stories.summary: This mobile spin-off maintains the gameplay loop and visuals of its console counterparts, with the caveat of how progress gates push microtransactions.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders Review
sources.text: If there's a singular idea that defines Monster Hunter, it's the grind. Capcom's mega-hit franchise, ever since its inception on the PSP, has flourished because of how it embraces the very idea of grinding and transforms it into an infectiously fun gameplay loop. Repetition and habit are vital parts of the series, so it makes sense, then, that the mobile game gacha format would eventually come to Monster Hunter, fitting currencies and timed gauges into that collecting and grinding experience. But my biggest surprise with Monster Hunter Outlanders has been how it's a comprehensive, full-fledged Monster Hunter packed onto phones and tablets. While it does eventually get buried under an avalanche of currencies to keep track of and some gacha roadblocks, there's enough meat on the bone here to sustain those hungry for more Monster Hunter or a solid action RPG on mobile. Like most Monster Hunter games, Outlanders follows a group of intrepid explorers from the Adventurer's Guild, this time sent to the uncharted island of Aesolan to investigate a mineral called Radiantate, and how it's influencing various breeds of monsters. After a brief action-packed intro, you're essentially let loose onto the island, free to explore the first environment or tackle the story as you see fit. But also, like most Monster Hunter games, the initial 20 or so hours of Outlanders are extremely guided and layered with seemingly endless tutorials. That's compounded by the nature of being a mobile game, meaning it has to introduce a half-dozen modes, various pull systems, currencies for powering up your Adventurer, and much more. The most succinct way to describe Outlanders is if you took Monster Hunter World , streamlined its combat, and crammed the entire thing into a mobile game. I almost cannot overstate how closely Outlanders resembles World in every way, even right down to the general structure and story. It takes a bit of an interesting approach, filling the story with a cast of characters that doubles as the big gacha pulls, even though you also have your "main" player-created character. While the overall story feels a bit rote and generic, the world of Outlanders itself is still brimming with things to do. While not a traditional open world game, it's in the exact same framework as Monster Hunter World and Wilds , giving you massive zones to explore. In these zones, you can naturally hunt monsters (without kicking off missions), gather resources, engage in little minigames like a rhythmic one where you steal a flying monster's treasure, and undertake any number of sidequests. My biggest surprise with Outlanders is how uncompromising the scope of its world feels, right in line with a big mainline Monster Hunter, supported by the fact that this game looks absolutely stunning, and runs like a dream. On an iPhone 14 Plus I was able to run the game on High settings with a stable 45fps, and almost zero slowdown, even during intense battles. The actual act of exploring the world feels just as entrancing as in major Monster Hunters. Various options for constructing camps and equipment as you explore the world make both traversal and item gathering easier. Camps unlock fast travel points and places to rest, catapults send your adventurer flying on their glider at high speed, and resource collectors constantly soak up those valuable items you need. Combat is still largely about that push-and-pull of timing, knowing when to pivot between offense and defense, and winding up your attacks at just the right time. That timing and weight of battle has always set Monster Hunter apart from other action games, and it's still present here. But where you can see the mobile limitations is in the particulars of combat control and the various, and many systems, used to improve your Adventurer's stats. Essentially, Outlanders is a squad-based Monster Hunter, where you build a party consisting of your main character and characters you pull (multiplayer with other actual players is available, too). But you can also play as each of the gacha characters, who have their own movesets, Ultimates, and abilities. For example, Keres uses dual blades that are actually a set of claws, giving her a completely separate set of skills, including one Wolverine-like drill attack. Meanwhile, Luxheart has a two-handed sword that he can rev up to shoot out fireworks, making each of his attacks like a miniature show. These various characters are actually one of my favorite parts of Outlanders, as their designs dig into a bit of tokusatsu pizazz , leaning into the overall goofiness of Monster Hunter as well. Having distinct movests also goes a long way to breaking up the monotony of repeat hunts and grinding. However, Outlanders overall has fewer weapon types than the last few games as a result, clocking in at eight total weapon types – some notable exclusions being the Hunting Horn and Insect Glaive. And overall, Outlanders plays a bit like a slightly simplified version of World in that it streamlines the more dynamic gameplay. For example, a lot of the emergent world elements, like using a Flashfly to stun a monster, are simple icons that pops up on-screen if you're near. The bigger change, however, is Outlander's two different control schemes: Adventure and Classic. Adventure boils everything down to three buttons – Attack, React, and Burst – automatically and intuitively altering each of these buttons based on the situation. As examples, the Bowgun will swap ammo based on what's most effective in the moment, or the react button might turn into a guard instead of a dodge. Classic control mode gives you more fine-tuned control with more dedicated buttons in the vein of a typical Monster Hunter experience. It works fine on a touchscreen, perhaps even a bit better than I was expecting. But if you opt to use touch controls, I'd heavily recommend the Adventure control scheme, simply because Classic is a lot to juggle without a gamepad-style attachment or acces

sources.title: Capcom quietly updates the Monster Hunter Wilds beta listing on Steam, indicating a possible expansion playtest
sources.text: We might get an early taste of Ascendance before long. Capcom still hasn't announced a release date for Monster Hunter Wilds : Ascendance, the Sunbreak-scale DLC that was revealed in February , but it seems like we might be getting a chance to sample the expansion before too long. A recent Steam listing update has provided a strong reason to suspect that there'll be a public beta for Ascendance available ahead of its launch in 2027. As SteamDB changelogs show, the Steam app entry for Monster Hunter Wilds' 2024 public beta was quietly updated early this morning to change the app's name from "Monster Hunter Wilds Beta test" to "Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test." Similarly, the listing's visual assets were updated to feature key art of a hunter facing an Arateka, one of the new monsters being introduced in the expansion. And sure enough, while the Wilds beta was removed from player libraries after it ended, it's possible for users who'd previously played it to confirm its listing changes within the Steam app by viewing their own played games from their Steam profile. I just looked. It says Ascendance right there. As the previous Wilds beta consisted of a repackaged demo build, it's likely that an Ascendance beta would follow suit: I'd expect a similar set of hunts to what in-person attendees were able to get hands-on time with at Tokyo Game Show in September, offering a chance to try out the new Boost Bracer weapon mechanics in Master Rank combat. If a beta does materialize, it'll hopefully be a smoother experience than what beta hunters got in 2024. The early Wilds playtest was the first time PC players encountered the dreaded origami monsters , a symptom of the severe optimization issues that tanked Wilds' reputation for over a year after launch. As for when that beta might be available, we can only speculate—but given that Monster Hunter has made prior appearances at Geoff Keighley productions, a public playtest that accompanies a hypothetical Game Awards trailer makes intuitive sense. But I'm just reading the tea leaves here—Capcom hasn't said a word about when it'll offer its next DLC teaser. Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance is set to launch some time in 2027. sources.title: Monster Hunter Wilds' upcoming Ascendance expansion may be getting a beta, some curious Steam backend updates suggest
sources.text: Monster Hunter Wilds 's first expansion, Ascendance, is set for release sometime next year . But, judging by some very suspect recent changes to the Wilds beta app on Steam, we may be playing some of the new stuff earlier than we thought. On Steam, Capcom quietly updated the Monster Hunter Wilds Beta app to now say Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test. You can see the change log on SteamDB (via PC Gamer ), which also shows an updated key art - all signs that point towards an impending beta for Ascendance. The beta app is the same one those who played the original Wilds beta had in their library. Though the app was removed following the beta's conclusion, because the two share the same ID, the beta should be visible in users' list of played games under the new name. This could mean players won't need to sign up for the supposed Ascendance beta, seemingly only needing to download the new client. Seeing as Ascendance itself doesn't have a release date, beyond a nebulous 2027 target, it's hard to speculate when Capcom plans to release the beta. Sometime early in 2027 would be a good guess, perhaps alongside a release date announcement. Capcom has shown off Ascendance on multiple occasions, more recently in Sony's September State of Play, where we got to see a number of the expansion's new features . A few days later at Tokyo Game Show, we got a first look at returning Elder Dragon Teostra , which we can hunt in the expansion. Capcom is keen for Ascendance to deliver the level of challenge Monster Hunter is known for, following feedback that the launch version of Wilds simply lacked that expected level of difficulty . While post-launch updates have certainly raised the level of challenge , Ascendance looks to be the next step up.
